absent: Locking, concurrency and sleeping rules for all described interfaces are not shown.
Error codes, permission checks and validation beyond range checks for ioctls and constructors are not shown.
Kernel side implementation, state transitions and side effects of console, coverage, compare, IPC, network and iommufd operations are not shown.
Definitions and values for kd symbols from kbdiacruc onward including wide accent, keycode, signal accept, repeat and font operation structures and ioctls were outside the routed range.
Exact numeric ioctl encodings for iommufd commands and detailed flag meanings and size negotiation for iommufd allocation structures are not shown.
Interpretation of IPv4 and IPv6 device configuration values and units is not shown.

findings.text: The virtual event queue allocation descriptor is a fixed eight word header where each slot is an unsigned 32 bit value. In order the slots convey the caller structure length, option flags, parent virtual unit handle, queue kind selector, requested depth, kernel assigned queue identifier, kernel assigned file handle, and a reserved word that stays zero.

The hardware queue allocation descriptor begins with five unsigned 32 bit words followed by two aligned 64 bit quantities. The leading words convey structure length, option flags, parent virtual handle, kind selector and index. The trailing quantities convey a nesting parent address and a byte length. The assigned queue identifier is returned through one of the leading words.
Hardware queue kinds use small integers. The default kind uses zero. The Tegra command queue virtualization kind uses one.

Tegra virtual command queues follow an ordered stack discipline. Creation proceeds upward starting at index zero. Teardown proceeds downward starting at the most recently created index. Out of order creation or removal is defined as failure.

Tegra queue memory must satisfy alignment and sizing rules. Its base aligns to its own byte length and is mapped in the associated address space. Its length is a power of two between thirty two bytes and a ceiling derived from the SMMU capability register. Contiguous or huge page backing with a capped emulated size field is recommended.
Two iommufd commands provide user entry for virtual event queue creation and hardware queue creation. Each is an ioctl of the iommufd family distinguished by its own command selector.

Priority packs class in upper bits and level plus hint in lower bits. The class field starts at bit thirteen. Eight classes exist. The class mask keeps the low three bits of the shifted value. The data mask keeps the low thirteen bits. A helper extracts the low part by masking.
Four regular classes are numbered from zero upward for none and realtime and best effort and idle. A separate sentinel with value seven marks an invalid priority.
Priority levels use three bits giving eight distinct steps. A mask preserves the low three bits. A helper extracts the level by masking. The best effort count equals the level count.
Priority targets are numbered one for process and two for process group and three for user. The normal priority value is four and the best effort normal equals it.

Hints occupy ten bits above the three level bits. The shift equals the level width. One thousand twenty four hint values exist. A mask preserves the ten bit field and a helper shifts then masks to extract it. Hint zero means no hint. Values one through seven request device duration limits of increasing index, effective only on devices supporting that feature where the hint selects the duration index.

A constructor validates class and level and hint against their counts and returns an invalid class marker shifted into place when any argument is negative or too large. Otherwise it composes the result by shifting the class and shifting the hint and merging the level.
An always inline helper in the user header builds a sixteen bit priority word from class and level and hint integers, with a macro alias providing the same construction.

The service wish mask equals 0x1E while the precedence mask equals 0xE0. Individual wishes use 0x10 for low delay and 0x08 for throughput and 0x04 for reliability and 0x02 for minimum cost. Precedence steps use 0x00 for routine and 0x20 for priority and 0x40 for immediate and 0x60 for flash and 0x80 for flash override and 0xA0 for critic and 0xC0 for internet control and 0xE0 for network control.

Option octets split into copy and class and number fields with masks 0x80 and 0x60 and 0x1F. Classes use 0x00 for control and 0x20 and 0x60 for reserved values and 0x40 for measurement. Named options combine class plus copy plus number to select end and no operation and security and loose source route and timestamp and CIPSO and record route and stream identifier and strict source route and router alert with number twenty. Version is four. Maximum lifetime is 255 with default 64. Offsets use zero for value and one for length and two for pointer with minimum pointer four and maximum option length forty. Aliases equate NOP with no operation and EOL with end and TS with timestamp. Timestamp modes use zero for time only and one for time plus address and three for prespecified. The BEET ceiling is eight.

The IPv4 header starts with a version nibble and length nibble whose order swaps with endian, followed by service octet, total length, identifier, fragment offset, lifetime, protocol, checksum, then source and destination addresses grouped together. Options follow the fixed part.

Authentication headers carry next header and length in 32 bit units plus reserved and security index and sequence with a variable authentication tail of at least four bytes respecting wide alignment. Security payload headers carry security index and sequence with a variable encrypted tail of at least eight bytes under the same alignment. Compression headers carry next header plus flags plus index. BEET headers carry next header plus header and pad lengths plus a reserved octet.

Packet aggregation headers carry a subtype octet plus flags plus block offset. The basic form uses subtype zero and the congestion control form uses subtype one and adds loss rate and round trip delay plus timing value and echo fields.
Several network headers end with flexible tails whose length is not fixed in the descriptor, requiring callers to size buffers from packet length rather than structure size.

Device configuration indexes start at one for forwarding and increase by one through multicast forwarding, proxy ARP, redirect handling, shared media, reverse path filtering, source route acceptance, boot relay, martian logging, tagging, ARP filtering, medium identifier, transform and policy bypasses, IGMP forcing, ARP announcement and ignore and accept and notify, secondary promotion, local acceptance, mark handling, VLAN proxy, localnet routing, IGMP intervals, linkdown handling, L2 multicast and gratuitous ARP drops, broadcast forwarding, and carrier based ARP eviction. The maximum equals the sentinel minus one.
The permission block orders its fields as key, user identifier, group identifier, creator user identifier, creator group identifier, mode, and sequence counter.

The private key uses zero. Creation flags use octal 1000 for create and 2000 for exclusive and 4000 for nonblocking, with 10000 for distributed and 20000 for owner. Control commands use zero for remove and one for set and two for status and three for info. Version selectors use zero for old and hex 0100 for wide capable.
The compatibility kludge holds a user space message buffer reference followed by a signed message type.

Multiplex numbers assign one to semaphore operation and two to semaphore creation and three to semaphore control and four to timed semaphore operation and eleven to message send and twelve to message receive and thirteen to message creation and fourteen to message control and twenty one to shared memory attach and twenty two to detach and twenty three to creation and twenty four to control and twenty five to distributed calls. A helper composes version and operation by placing version in the high sixteen bits.
The compatibility kludge holds a user space pointer that must be validated before dereference.
Minimum IPv6 message size is 1280.
Packet info pairs an IPv6 address with an interface index. MTU info pairs a socket address with a 32 bit MTU. Interface requests order an address then a 32 bit prefix length then an interface index.
The strict flag uses one. Routing types use zero for deprecated type zero and two for type two and three for type three and four for type four. Strict and type zero are marked for removal.

Routing headers sequence next header and header length and routing type and segments left before type specific variable data. Option headers sequence next header and length before encoded options and carry a packed attribute. Destination and hop by hop headers reuse the option shape.
The router alert option value for multicast listener discovery equals zero.

Type zero routing headers append a reserved word and a flexible address array to the generic header with an alias exposing the type field. Type two headers append a reserved word and a single address with a similar type alias. Home address options sequence an eight bit type and length before an address and use packed layout. The base IPv6 header starts with version and priority nibbles whose order swaps by endian, followed by a three octet flow label, payload length, next header, hop limit, then source and destination addresses grouped together.
Routing type zero ends with a flexible address array and option headers carry variable option data, so fixed size handling truncates.

IPv6 device settings form a zero based sequential enumeration beginning with forwarding and covering hop limit, MTU, advertisement acceptance and timing, autoconfiguration, duplicate detection, temporary addresses and lifetimes, address limits, multicast forcing, proxy ND, optimistic handling, source route acceptance, disable flag, notification, report intervals, fragment handling, local advertisement handling, secret and mode selectors, linkdown handling, multicast and solicitation drops, address retention, solicitation intervals, segment routing and HMAC, enhanced detection, policy disable, traffic class, RPL and measurement toggles plus identifiers, carrier eviction, untracked handling, minimum lifetimes, and forced forwarding, ending with a maximum sentinel.

Kernel compare selectors use zero for file and one for virtual memory and two for file tables and three for filesystem and four for signal handlers and five for input output and six for semaphore sets and seven for epoll targets, with a final count sentinel.
Epoll comparison slots order three 32 bit words for the epoll descriptor and the target descriptor number and the offset within same numbered sequences.
Remote coverage arguments order trace mode, buffer length in words, handle count, a common aligned 64 bit handle, then a flexible handle array.

At most 256 remote handles are allowed. The four controls share type c with numbers one for trace initialization and one hundred for enable and one hundred one for disable and one hundred two for remote enable. Initialization reads a word while remote enable writes the argument structure.
Program counter tracing uses zero to keep older callers working while comparison operand tracing uses one.

Comparison encoding reserves bit zero for constant marking and shifts size left one with a mask covering three. Subsystem tags place zero for common and one for USB in the top byte. Masks isolate the top byte for subsystem and the low 32 bits for instance.
The remote argument ends with a flexible handle array whose true size comes from the count field, so fixed size copies truncate or overrun.
Font descriptors order character count and character height as sixteen bit values followed by a user pointer to expanded font data. Counts of 256 or 512 and heights 1 through 32 are documented.

Font ioctls use 0x4B60 for getting and 0x4B61 for setting expanded fonts and 0x4B6B and 0x4B6C for descriptor based get and set with 0x4B6D for reset. Palette ioctls use 0x4B70 for get and 0x4B71 for set. Sound uses 0x4B2F with zero meaning off and tone uses 0x4B30.

LED ioctls use 0x4B31 for get and 0x4B32 for set with bits 0x01 for scroll and 0x02 for num and 0x04 for caps. Keyboard type query uses 0x4B33 with answers 0x01 for 84 key and 0x02 for 101 key and 0x03 for other. Port ioctls use 0x4B34 through 0x4B37 for add and remove and video enable and disable. Mode set uses 0x4B3A with zero for text and one for graphics plus two and three for obsolete text modes, while mode get uses 0x4B3B. Display mapping uses 0x4B3C for map and 0x4B3D for unmap.

Screen entries are single bytes. Unicode pairs order a sixteen bit code point before a sixteen bit font position. Mapping descriptors order a sixteen bit entry count before a user pointer to pairs. Initialization hints order three sixteen bit advices for hash size and step and level where zero means no opinion.

Unicode map ioctls use 0x4B66 for get and 0x4B67 for set and 0x4B68 for clear. The direct mapped font area starts at 0xF000 with mask 0x01FF. Tab size is 256. Narrow screen map ioctls use 0x4B40 and 0x4B41 while full Unicode screen map ioctls use 0x4B69 and 0x4B6A.

Keyboard modes use zero for raw and one for translate and two for medium raw and three for Unicode and four for off, with get 0x4B44 and set 0x4B45. Meta handling uses 0x03 for bit and 0x04 for escape prefix, with get 0x4B62 and set 0x4B63. Lock flags use 0x01 for scroll and 0x02 for num and 0x04 for caps, with get 0x4B64 and set 0x4B65 for flags rather than lights.

Key entries order table and index bytes before a sixteen bit value. Function key entries order a function byte before a 512 byte string. Accent entries order diacritic and base and result bytes. Accent tables order a 32 bit count before 256 entries.

Key tables use zero for normal and one for shift and two for alt and three for alt shift, with get 0x4B46 and set 0x4B47. Function strings use get 0x4B48 and set 0x4B49. Accent tables use get 0x4B4A and set 0x4B4B.
Font data and unicode map descriptors carry user pointers plus counts, so handling must validate user memory and entry counts.

Console ioctls provide user entry for font, palette, sound, indicators, keyboard type, port permissions, video mode, display mapping, screen maps, unicode maps, keyboard mode, meta handling, lock flags, key translation, function strings and accent tables.
Both IP and IPv6 base headers swap the order of two four bit fields based on little versus big endian bitfield macros and fail compilation when neither is defined.
Small helpers extract option copy and class and number by masking the option octet, and extract service wishes and precedence by masking the service octet.
Each routed user header establishes a single inclusion guard that prevents double inclusion.
